corrections.wrong: "out of range it read the default `meminst`, whose byte list is empty". The old `fun_mem` is `s.MEMS[f.MODULE.MEMS[x]!]!`. An out-of-range module index gives the default address 0 (memaddr = Nat), and that then reads `S.mems[0]`, which is a real memory whenever the store has one. Only an out-of-range store address gives the default meminst (`(default : meminst).BYTES = []`, as the old `mem_bytes_wf` uses).
corrections.fixed: "...was always defined, because each out-of-range `!` lookup returned a default: address `0` from the module's list, or, from the store, the default `meminst`, whose byte list is empty."

corrections.wrong: "`subst Hcontext` makes `C.mems` literally `C'.mems`". After the subst, `Hlen` is about `(upd_local_label_return C' ...).MEMS`. That is only definitionally equal to `C'.MEMS`, and `fun_mem_typed ... Hlen` is accepted by defeq.
corrections.fixed: "makes `C.mems` definitionally `C'.mems` (`upd_local_label_return` changes only locals, labels and return), so `Hlen` serves as the bound for `C'`."

corrections.wrong: "`obtain ⟨mi, Hmem⟩ := ⟨_, fun_mem_typed ...⟩`, so `Hmem : fun_mem (s;f) 0 mi` with `mi = S.mems[F.module.memaddrs[0]]`". This suggests the proof has that equation. The real code obtains from an ascribed `∃ mi, fun_mem ... mi`, so `mi` is a fresh opaque variable. The text also left out the ascription.
corrections.fixed: Shows the ascription `obtain ⟨mi, Hmem⟩ : ∃ mi, fun_mem (s;f) 0 mi := ⟨_, ...⟩` and says the existential hides that `mi` is `S.mems[F.module.memaddrs[0]]`, so every fact about `mi` comes from `Hmem`.

corrections.wrong: "Lean `VLOAD V128 (SHAPE M X N sx)`". That is spec notation. The Lean constructor is `vloadop_.SHAPEX_ (sz.mk_sz v_M) v_N v_sx`.
corrections.fixed: "Lean `VLOAD V128 (SHAPEX_ M N sx)`", the same abbreviation style the section uses for SPLAT/ZERO.

corrections.wrong: "So the instruction always steps to `with_mem (s;f) 0 (n1+offset) 16 b*`". This reads as a deterministic claim. In the model, `Step.vstore_oob` also applies out of bounds; what holds is that `vstore_val` is always available.
corrections.fixed: "So `Step.vstore_val` always applies, even out of bounds (where `Step.vstore_oob` applies too), and steps to `with_mem ...` with an empty instruction sequence."

corrections.wrong: "No bounds are needed, so the instruction never traps." This is false. Out of bounds, `Step.vstore_lane_oob` also applies, so the instruction can trap. The lemma just never needs the trap rule.
corrections.fixed: "The rule has no memory-bounds premise and `with_mem` was total, so this step exists even out of bounds, where `Step.vstore_lane_oob` also applies. The lemma therefore needs no trap case."
